learn.title: The round shape
learn.body: A circle is all points at a fixed distance, the radius $r$, from a centre. The diameter $d$ goes through the centre and equals $2r$. The distance around the circle is the circumference.

learn.title: The number pi
learn.body: For every circle, circumference divided by diameter is the same number, $\pi\approx3.14159$. So $C=\pi d=2\pi r$. The area is $A=\pi r^2$. Notice the area uses $r$ squared, as area always scales with length squared.

learn.title: Circle calculations
learn.body: Leave answers in terms of $\pi$, then approximate.
Writing $25\pi$ is exact. Writing $78.5$ is rounded. Give the exact form unless a decimal is asked for.

questions.prompt: The radius of a circle is 5. What is its diameter?
questions.explanation: The diameter is twice the radius.

questions.prompt: A circle has radius 4. Its area is $k\pi$. Find $k$.
A circle has diameter 12. Its circumference is $k\pi$. Find $k$.

questions.explanation: Two times pi times the radius, which equals pi times the diameter.

questions.prompt: A circle has radius 5. What is its area, rounded to one decimal?
A circle has circumference $18\pi$. Find its radius.
The radius of a circle doubles. What happens to its area?
questions.explanation: Area grows with $r^2$, so doubling $r$ gives $4$ times the area.

questions.prompt: A circle has area $36\pi$. Find its radius.
